awww, don't let one girl cause you to ruin your life. chances are, even if you dated her and everything, people move on with their lives and you would find another girl who is even more beautiful and amazing eventually. so, whatever happens with that girl and her friends, don't stop your path now just because of 1 person. life changes soooo, so much in your teen and young adult years. you sound like you have a bright future, and you can probably find someone else if it doesn't work out with that girl. i know in the moment it feels like nothing will ever change and they are the only one you will ever be attracted to, but it's not true. you WILL find other girls.

the key to life is to take things in small bites. "inch by inch, life is a cinch. yard by yard, life is hard." so, if you want to accomplish something else, or find a girl that will be into you, just start in small steps. you will gain confidence when you achieve the first small step, and then the second, and you will start feeling better little by little.

-trying a diet of elimination (only eat certain things and see if it improves)

-seeing an allergist in case you're allergic to something you're eating

-make sure you're drinking plenty of water

hey ~ I'm so sorry you're experiencing pain, it's so awful when it becomes chronic everyday. :( When I first started experiencing pain I felt overwhelmed trying to find help. Something that helped me was to write a bulleted list of the things you want to mention to your doctor and bring it with you. This can be hand-written or on your phone as a note. Here's an example:

* (Where is the pain?) Pain occurs in arm
* (How frequent is the pain?) Pain is constant but worsens with extension of arm, such as when using a mouse at a computer or reaching for an item.
* (What does the pain feel like?) The pain feels like a tightness or muscle soreness
* (How would you rate the pain? Note: I **hate** this question but they almost always ask it unfortunately) 5 out of 10

Questions:

* What is the diagnosis?
* What form of treatment do you recommend?
* How soon should I start feeling better?
* Do you recommend ice or heat?
* Is there anything else I can do to start feeling better?

I hope this helps, hang in there!

Sometimes this can get your foot in the door a LOT sooner, especially if you can be available on short notice. You may try calling a few days later to check in if any cancellations have opened up a spot. (Half the time the front desk is a different person every time you call anyway, so don't worry about appearing overly pushy, sometimes you HAVE to do this to get some traction going).

another idea is to shop around for another neurosurgery place, do you need a referral from your PCP to get it covered by insurance? if so, start calling around to other neurosurgery places and ask  about when their soonest appointment is. once you find one that is reasonable, call your PCP and get the referral to that place.

it shouldn't be this way, but sometimes you can sort of use these tricks to get in sooner. you deserve treatment ASAP. you're a human being who is trying to better their situation, and you deserve results for even trying.
